listenPorts.why: Remote Desktop is listening. Exposed RDP is a leading brute-force and ransomware entry point; require NLA and never expose it directly.
SMB is listening. SMB is the primary lateral-movement channel on Windows networks and a ransomware target.
Telnet is listening. Credentials cross the wire in plaintext.
FTP is listening. Credentials and data are unencrypted.
VNC is listening. Many builds ship with weak or absent authentication.
Redis is listening. Unauthenticated Redis is routinely abused for remote code execution.
MongoDB is listening. Check authentication and bind address.
Elasticsearch is listening. Historically deployed without authentication.
Memcached is listening. Abused for amplification and cache poisoning.
Legacy NetBIOS session service is listening.
SSH is listening. Confirm it is intentional and key-only.
MSSQL is listening on the network.
MySQL is listening on the network.
PostgreSQL is listening on the network.
WinRM over HTTP is listening; remote management traffic is unencrypted.

remotePorts.why: Outbound to 4444, the default Metasploit handler port.
Outbound to 4445, a common reverse-shell handler port.
Outbound to 31337, a classic backdoor port.
Outbound to 1337, frequently used by commodity backdoors.
Outbound IRC; some botnets use IRC for command and control.
Outbound to 6666, frequently used by remote-access trojans.
Outbound SOCKS proxy port; could be tunnelling.
Outbound Tor SOCKS port; confirm the anonymiser is sanctioned.
TeamViewer relay port; confirm the remote-access tool is sanctioned.

egressWatch.why: certutil should not transfer files. -urlcache, -split, -verifyctl and -decode are the documented download and deobfuscation arguments. Capture the destination and the command line.
BITS is a download primitive that can survive reboot and run a notify command. The transfer itself usually runs inside svchost.exe, so also watch BITS-Client job events.
mshta has no normal reason to reach the internet. Remote HTA content is proxy execution.
regsvr32 fetching a remote scriptlet is the documented squiblydoo pattern.
A logon script host opening an internet socket is abnormal outside a managed script window.
cscript performing its own download is a scripting-host egress pattern.
rundll32 egress almost always means DLL code with a network role; correlate with the loaded module.
An MSI pulled from the internet and installed quietly.
Managed code running under InstallUtil and beaconing.
MSBuild performing network activity outside a build agent.
forfiles is an indirect-execution wrapper; egress from it or its child is suspicious.
Compatibility Assistant proxy execution with a network leg.
cmstp installing a profile and reaching the network.
ODBC setup utility loading a DLL that talks to the network.
COM verification host with a network leg.
Wizard host with a network leg.
Compiled help viewer reaching the network.
Control panel applet with a network leg.
wmic toward a peer over RPC is the lateral-movement leg; correlate with 4688 on the target.
